key_insight: The main weakness of frontier LLMs in this study was not medical knowledge, but failing to actively seek the right information under uncertainty.
clinical_relevance: For clinical oncology, this means a model can sound reasoned yet still miss key data needed for diagnosis and treatment decisions.
method: 32 frontier models were tested in an agentic hematologic oncology evaluation.
Models had to request clinical data across 3 sequential rounds before giving a diagnosis and treatment plan.
Performance was assessed with accuracy, information utilization, and a clinical reasoning rubric.
evidence_signal: The best model reached 68% overall accuracy, and information utilization strongly predicted accuracy (R = 0.69, P < 0.001), while utilization dropped from 57% to 26% in the final round.
watch_item: This framework highlights a major implementation risk: apparently strong reasoning traces may mask incomplete data gathering, so deployment should not rely on explanation quality alone.
paper_title: Information-seeking failures of large language models in agentic clinical reasoning
